modules.transcript: Student: Hello, I’m looking for books for my biology assignment. Librarian: Sure. What topic are you studying? Student: It’s about plant growth and how plants develop. Librarian: You can find beginner-level books in the biology section on the second floor. Student: Is there a specific shelf I should look for? Librarian: Yes, look for the shelf labeled 'Plant Science.' ■ Student: Do the books have pictures and diagrams? Librarian: Most of them do. ■ They are very helpful for understanding. Student: How long can I borrow the books? Librarian: The borrowing period is fourteen days. ■ Student: Can I renew them if I need more time? Librarian: Yes, you can renew them online before the due date. Student: Thank you so much for your help. Librarian: You’re welcome.
modules.insertSentence: These visual aids make complex topics easier to understand for students.

modules.transcript: Professor: Which part is difficult for you? Student: I don’t understand the difference between producers and consumers. Professor: Producers are organisms like plants that make their own food. ■ Consumers depend on other organisms for food. ■ Student: That helps a lot. Do we need to write examples? Professor: Yes, include at least two examples for each group. ■ Student: When is the homework due? Professor: It’s due on Friday at noon. Student: Can I submit it online? Professor: Yes, submit it through the course portal. Student: Thank you, Professor. Professor: You’re welcome.
modules.insertSentence: Understanding the difference is important for completing your assignment correctly.

modules.transcript: Student A: Have you finished your part of the group project yet? Student B: Not completely. I’m still working on the timeline section. Student A: The project is due tomorrow morning, so we don’t have much time. Student B: I know. I plan to finish my work tonight. Student A: That’s good. I’ve already written the introduction, but it needs some editing. ■ Student B: I can help you review it if you want. Student A: That would be great. Thank you. Student B: Why don’t we meet in the library this evening? Student A: Sure. What time should we meet? Student B: Let’s meet at six p.m. Student A: Perfect. See you then.
modules.insertSentence: It’s important that we turn in a polished project because it affects our final grade.

modules.transcript: Student: Hi, I'd like to join the photography club. Office Staff: That's great. You can sign up through the student activities website. Student: Are there any requirements to join? Office Staff: No, the club is open to all students. Student: Do I need to attend a meeting? Office Staff: Yes, you must attend the first meeting. Student: When is that? Office Staff: Next Tuesday at four p.m. in Room B204. Student: Do I need to bring my camera? Office Staff: Not for the first meeting. ■ They'll discuss equipment later. Student: Is there a membership fee? Office Staff: Yes, it's two hundred rupees for the semester. Student: Okay, thank you for the information. Office Staff: You're welcome.
modules.insertSentence: The first session will mainly explain how the club works and what members can expect.

modules.transcript: Student: Hi, what is today’s special meal? Cafeteria Worker: Today we have vegetable pasta and grilled chicken. Student: Does the pasta contain any dairy products? Cafeteria Worker: Yes, it contains cheese. Student: I’m lactose intolerant. Is there another option? Cafeteria Worker: You can try the grilled chicken. Student: What comes with the chicken meal? Cafeteria Worker: It comes with rice and a small salad. Student: How much does it cost? Cafeteria Worker: It costs one hundred and twenty rupees. Student: Can I pay using my card? Cafeteria Worker: Yes, we accept card and digital payments. Student: Great, I’ll take the chicken meal. Cafeteria Worker: Sure. ■ It’ll be ready shortly.
modules.insertSentence: Many students choose this option because it is a healthier choice.
